ai_analysis.summary: A promotional post announces a PDF about using SQL CASE WHEN in real-time analytics, framed around a real interview question said to have been asked at Walmart and ZS Associates. It says the PDF covers customer segmentation for millions of users, SQL-based business logic, performance optimization, and cleaner, audit-friendly ETL, BI, and analytics pipelines, with a claimed telco example involving 20 million users and daily segmentation. The supplied content contains no PDF text, SQL code, segmentation rules, optimization techniques, or supporting measurements, so those details cannot be evaluated from this post.
subtopics: Customer segmentation for millions of users
Daily segmentation in a claimed 20-million-user telco example
Reducing compute by pushing business logic into SQL
Centralizing logic across ETL, BI, and analytics

interview_questions.question: What role does the post say SQL CASE WHEN plays in large-scale customer segmentation?
interview_questions.answer:
The post presents CASE WHEN as a strategic SQL mechanism for implementing customer segmentation for millions of users.
The answer should acknowledge that the post does not provide the segmentation conditions, categories, or SQL implementation.

interview_questions.question: What pipeline-design benefits does the post associate with pushing business logic into SQL?
interview_questions.answer:
Centralizing business logic in SQL allows it to be shared across ETL, BI, and analytics workflows.
The post claims this approach can reduce pipeline complexity and compute use while improving dashboard load times.
It also associates the approach with cleaner, audit-friendly pipelines, but it does not provide implementation or measurement details.
